summary: Compare the coefficients of u^k. Θ_f(u·a·v) is an integral of f against exp(u·L(w)) with L the linear form w ↦ a∑_p⟨w_p, v_p⟩; expanding the exponential and exchanging sum and integral (dominated convergence) gives its power series; k! times the k-th coefficient of either side is the jet of T_a f along (∑ v_i z_i)^k: jet((∑_i v_i z_i)^k, F) = k!·[u^k]F(u·v) (a jet along a monomial z^α carries the factor α!, ZerosCostDegree.lean 162).

steps.claim: It suffices to compare, for each k, the coefficients of u^k.
Let L be the continuous ℂ-linear form w ↦ a·∑_p ⟨w_p, v_p⟩ on Fock coordinates.
steps.lean: let L := a • ∑ p, innerSLFlip ℂ (v p) ∘SL .proj p

steps.claim: Two facts. (a) The function t ↦ Θ_f(t·a·v) has at 0 the power series with coefficients ∫ realVac(w)·f(realVec w)·L(w)^k/k! dμ(w): its value at every t is the integral of realVac(w) f(realVec w) e^{tL(w)}, and the exponential series can be summed under the integral by dominated convergence (|L(w)| ≤ ‖L‖‖w‖, ∫ e^{c‖w‖}·realVac integrable); hence k! times its k-th Taylor coefficient is that integral. (b) k! times the coefficient of u^k of the substituted series T_a f(v·u) equals the jet of T_a f along the polynomial (∑_i v_i z_i)^k (`jet_subst_linearSeries` turns the jet of the substituted series along X^k, which is k!·[u^k], into that jet).
steps.lean:

    .mul_right
    (realVac w * f (realVec w)) (expSeries_div_hasSum_exp (t * L w))))).choose_spec.factorial_smul 1
    k, (jet_subst_linearSeries (.replicateCol _ v) (.X () ^ k) (V.jetSeries a f)).symm
steps.indivisible: one `rcases` of a pair of terms; the first is a single application of `hasFPowerSeriesAt_iff` to one application of `hasSum_integral_of_dominated_convergence`, whose nine lines are that lemma's hypotheses (measurability, domination, summability, integrability, pointwise sum)
